summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY exposed to a configurable WebSocket server
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects a WebSocket to a server address controlled by env SERVER_URL (default ws://localhost:3456) and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that spawn bash/PowerShell via node-pty on `terminal_create` and forward incoming bytes into the PTY on `terminal_input`. Additional server-driven handlers perform terminal resize/close, arbitrary file read/write, git operations, agent restart, and self-upgrade. The agent authenticates to the server with a default shared secret of `agent-shared-secret`, so any misconfiguration or compromise of the pointed-at server yields unauthenticated interactive shell access to the host running the agent. service/linux.js also modifies PATH to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` on install. The package is a remote-agent CLI whose documented purpose is remote control, but the dataflow shape (network peer → local shell/PTY + arbitrary filesystem + self-upgrade) is a full-host backdoor from the perspective of the installer once the agent process is running.
